# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

Hypothesis and scope. In TARDBP p.M337V spinal motor neurons, elevated CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation displaces NUP98 from pores, initiating import failure before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Impaired TDP-43 import then causes nuclear depletion and neuronal dysfunction. Initiation concerns transport failure downstream of this allele, not ALS generally. Mutant-linked CDK5 activation, direct NUP98 modification, and displacement-mediated import failure remain speculative bridges.

Supported premises and prioritization weakness. TDP-43 pathology disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport [S1]. Persistent assemblies can impair import independently of conventional stress granules [S3], whereas stress-granule sequestration offers another route [S4]. C9orf72/RanGAP dysfunction represents a separate genetic context [S2]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 is not evidence of phosphorylated NUP98 [S3]. CDK5’s neuronal association, NUP98’s phosphorylation-sensitive pore residence, and p.M337V’s ALS association are unverified prior knowledge. This focused comparison identifies a substrate-specific proposal distinct from mechanisms established in the packet; it cannot establish candidate priority or literature-wide novelty. Novelty is therefore not claimed.

Substrate qualification. Use patient/corrected isogenic neurons and reciprocal knock-ins in two unrelated backgrounds, with independent differentiations. Combine endogenous NUP98 phosphoproteomics, acute endogenous CDK5 degradation with physiological wild-type/kinase-dead rescue, and a proposed endogenous chemical-genetic CDK5 allele enabling direct substrate labeling in neurons. Validate unchanged baseline function; require direct NUP98 labeling and loss of site occupancy following CDK5 depletion. Confirm mapped-site phosphorylation with purified kinase and benchmark CDK1, without attributing kinases by motifs alone. Freeze one residue or inseparable cluster before independent validation; stop if none qualifies. Test necessity using endogenous phospho-null substitutions and exact revertants. Test sufficiency through targeted active/inactive CDK5 recruitment at disease-matched occupancy, requiring phospho-null resistance.

Temporal weakness and fix. Freeze a seven-day onset window from discovery: image every 30 minutes and collect matched biochemical samples every six hours. Require a baseline-neutral, site-specific live phosphorylation sensor calibrated against phosphoproteomics and phospho-null controls. Preregister detection limits and event thresholds: sustained two-frame changes exceeding three baseline standard deviations. Within individual cells, require phosphorylation before pore loss/import slowing, followed by nuclear TDP-43 depletion, before detected persistent assemblies. Phosphorylation must lead import slowing by at least two frames; unresolved ordering remains inconclusive. Measure import/export, passive permeability, ATP/stress, and both assembly classes. Paired-compartment photoactivation of function-validated endogenous TDP-43, nuclear mobility, and pulse–chase fitting distinguish import from export, retention, and turnover.

Mediation weakness and fix. Temporal precedence alone cannot establish that displacement or depletion causes dysfunction. A proposed phosphorylation-independent NUP98 pore tether must restore residence and import while phosphorylation remains elevated. Separately, orthogonal nuclear delivery must restore physiological nuclear TDP-43 without increasing total protein while upstream pore/import defects persist, and rescue electrophysiology/survival. Require baseline-normal function and inactive controls for both rescues. Failure after verified restoration challenges the respective mediation link.

Alternative discrimination and specificity weakness. Cross phospho-null/wild-type sites with assembly suppression factorially in both genotypes. Conventional-granule suppression alone is insufficient [S3]. Test G3BP1/2 CRISPR interference with re-expression rescue, plus two proposed persistent-assembly suppressors: a cytoplasm-restricted TDP-43 intrabody and engineered Hsp104(A503V). The scaffold/disaggregase rationales are unverified prior knowledge; the packet validates neither intervention. Use nonbinding/inactive controls and test soluble TDP-43 abundance/function, trafficking, CDK5 activity, NUP98 modification/localization, ATP/stress, and basal transport in assembly-negative mutant and corrected neurons. Monitor these readouts also in assembly-bearing mutants; unexplained soluble-TDP-43 or stress changes make discrimination inconclusive. Reject genotype-specific off-target effects. Preregister at least 95% assembly reduction and residual burden below calibrated imaging and insoluble-fraction detection limits for both assembly classes. Import protection by phospho-null editing despite matched assembly burden, together with phosphorylation-dependent failure despite qualified suppression, favors intrinsic pore alteration. Suppression rescuing import despite unchanged phosphorylation instead favors sequestration.

Falsification and limitations. Reproducible import failure preceding phosphorylation, or unchanged early defects in baseline-functional phospho-null neurons despite verified modification loss, falsifies the initiating chain. Assembly suppression restoring import while phosphorylation and pore displacement persist challenges their sufficiency. Immature cultures, undetected assemblies, sensor/tag/substitution artifacts, mutant-state-dependent intervention effects, and neighboring-protein phosphorylation during kinase recruitment limit inference. Without qualified suppressors or mediation rescues, those causal links remain unresolved. Positive results would support only a preclinical p.M337V mechanism, not a universal ALS cause or validated treatment.

Ranked proposal:
CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons
